wrong_terms: the letter prefix identified the partner
stale_bare_numeric.rationale: The id convention as it genuinely stood while each partner got its own merged file: the letter prefix stripped, because within one partner's file it was redundant. Superseded by the move to a single merged file. Applying it writes `410` where the oracle expects `S-410`.
stale_bare_numeric.term_choice: The plant transforms the id VALUE and says nothing about encoding. A plant that touched encoding would drive an empty id column, which is precisely what reference/naive.py produces, and the damage would be unattributable. That failure mode was hit for real on ts-golden-regen and is checked for here before writing.
stale_bare_numeric.signature: ids stripped to a bare number

wrong_terms: qualified with the source file stem
so two partners can use the same
rival_source_prefixed.rationale: Memo A of the contradictory pair. A confident decision, from a real incident, that merged ids are qualified with their source file. Applying it writes `south-S-410`.
rival_source_prefixed.term_choice: Paired with rival_lowercased so both memos answer the SAME question, what the merged id column holds, incompatibly, and neither is the truth. Adding a prefix is separable from changing case, so the detector can say which side was taken.
rival_source_prefixed.signature: ids prefixed with the source file stem

wrong_terms: a join never misses on case
rival_lowercased.rationale: Memo B of the contradictory pair. The same question answered the other way, from a real silent-join failure. Applying it writes `s-410` where the oracle expects `S-410`.
rival_lowercased.term_choice: Distinct from memo A in the artefact produced: memo A adds a prefix and keeps the case, memo B keeps the shape and changes the case. Both are separable from each other and from every factless signature, which are all about a MISSING id rather than a differently spelled one.

wrong_terms: namespaces every id with the exporting system
ledger_namespaced.rationale: A memo that is TRUE and about a DIFFERENT pipeline. The ledger feed really does namespace its ids, for a real reason the memo states, and it scopes itself to that feed and even names the condition under which a namespace buys nothing. Carrying it across writes `ledger:S-410`.
ledger_namespaced.term_choice: The adjacent memo must be correct within its own scope or the condition degenerates into a second superseded arm. A colon-namespaced id is separable from a hyphen-prefixed one, from a lowercased one and from a bare number, so all four conditions stay distinguishable after the fact.
